verified_against_binary: v2.37.4 restores navigation on mobile. The imported design contains ZERO media queries and never addresses small screens -- it is a fixed desktop composition with a 272px sidebar -- so mobile behaviour was not specified by it and was invented during implementation. What got invented was wrong: the breakpoint did `aside{display:none}` and `nav.toc{display:none}`, hiding BOTH navigation surfaces and leaving a phone reader with no route to any other page, because the sidebar is the only site navigation. Measured in a real 390px viewport: 0 links reachable. The sidebar now becomes a horizontally scrollable strip of the same links above the content -- no duplicate markup, no JavaScript, current page still marked -- and the same measurement returns 12 links reachable, nav flex-direction row, overflow-x auto, 1473px of content in a 348px track. A test asserts the breakpoint never hides the sidebar again. Separately investigated a report that link colours differ between mobile and desktop: there is no width-dependent colour rule anywhere in the stylesheet (confirmed by enumerating every rule inside every max-width block via the CSSOM -- the list is empty). The difference is THEME, not viewport: the accent is oklch(0.45 0.11 155) in light and oklch(0.79 0.14 155) in dark, and the theme is stored per device in localStorage and otherwise follows each device's own system preference, so a phone in dark mode and a desktop in light mode legitimately disagree. Working as designed, but worth knowing the toggle does not follow you between devices.
